cells.tense: You can feel toward something before it has a shape, and the freshness is still here.
cells.act: keep the motivation warm with steady care
cells.ask: Stay near whatever you keep circling back to — a little each day this week, small and regular instead of a burst. Keep it warm. Don't decide yet what it will become.
cells.core:
Something in you can move toward a thing before you can say what the thing is, and that earlier stage isn't fog. It's how this part of you works. What's left to do is let direction come from being interested rather than from being sure.

So stay near the same pull. Feeding it is the part that belongs to you; checking it can wait. Most people who build anything are still deciding what they're building. The warm version and the named version are the same thing at different depths. If you keep coming back to it, that isn't drifting — it's alive, and coming back is what keeping it alive looks like.

cells.tense: The next move hasn't happened yet and you're already living inside how it could go wrong.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Put the larger dream down for a week. Care for one real small thing instead — a plant, a shelf, a meal you actually cook. Notice what it needs and let its pace set yours.
cells.core:
Ahead of you, something hasn't happened yet, and you have already played every branch of how it goes — often alone, often far past where anything actually is. That's how this one bends under pressure: imagining into the gap where nothing has happened and no one is keeping you company in there.

It works when the dreaming has something solid to push against. Without the solid part, the mind starts making conditions instead of direction. So stay close to something you can water. When you keep one real small thing alive and watch what it needs, the large feeling comes back through a door you can walk through, not a window you keep looking in. The pace you learned there is the pace to trust for the large one too.

cells.tense: Something that used to move you has gotten quiet, and you keep the door shut rather than opening it.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Find a question that won't help you and follow it for an afternoon. Read one thing about it, tell no one, then set it down without deciding anything. Try this more than once.
cells.core:
The quiet is here, and you protect it by not asking it questions. What you feel toward new things doesn't come forward. You are farther back than the moment is.

This isn't a depth problem, it's a supply problem. The route back isn't to feel harder; it's to be interested without a reason. Curiosity is the younger form of what you already do well — the same line, run before it knows what it's for. Baby steps toward things you can't use is the right size. Nothing here needs solving. An afternoon on something useless, then let it drop. The next question will find you the same way.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking the questions that lead nowhere.

cells.tense: You go to abstract places to think clearly, then describe that as drifting off.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Next time a mess won't resolve, take a page and write the events in order — just what happened, no feelings in the sentences. Read it back and see the shape you already made.
cells.core:
You take what's around you and strip it down to how it works. Some of that is your way of being useful. You can look at a situation and see the structure holding it up, then tell the story as if you just happened to be there.

Somewhere along the way, seeing the pattern got filed as going somewhere else — overthinking, or a mode that isn't really yours. The people watching you don't experience it that way. They see someone who can find the shape in a mess and stay grounded while doing it. Whatever else this is, it's a way of being present. Not a way of leaving the room.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person deliberately guards a quiet, which the record does not show — the core only locates the capacity running empty, never the reason. The reader could reasonably object 'I'm not guarded, I just don't perform feeling in front of people I don't trust' — so the core names what the capacity is doing, not a motive, and can be refused and still be used. The asks survive a wrong read: curiosity followed for its own sake, attending to a small real thing, feeling toward what has no shape yet, and putting a mess onto paper are each worth doing whether or not the diagnosis lands. The line that serves the writer more than the person is the balanced close about 'nothing here to solve' — it is neat enough to admire itself — so I broke it apart before writing. The tenses are rephrased, not pasted; no card name reaches the glass; the four asks move on four different verbs and three different shapes.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person guards a quiet on purpose — the record only shows a capacity running empty, never the reason, so the core locates where they stand without saying why. A reader could reasonably object 'I'm not withdrawn, I just don't perform feeling for people I don't trust' — the core names what the capacity is doing, not a motive, and can be refused and still used. The asks survive a wrong read: each is worth doing on its own terms. The tense lines are paraphrased in the cores, not pasted; the four asks move on four different verbs and four different shapes — a practice, a bounded tending, a re-do, a noticing left alone.
